 Contract Ownership & Management  
 Own the end-to-end lifecycle of these contract vehicles, including onboarding, pricing schedules, modifications, options, renewals, and close-out. 
 Act as the subject-matter expert and primary point of contact for these contract vehicles across the organization. 
 Ensure ongoing compliance with contract terms, eligibility rules, and reporting obligations specific to each vehicle. 
 Maintain accurate, audit-ready contract documentation, pricing schedules, and records. 
 Current-State Assessment & Program Maturity  
 Assess how these contracts are currently sold, tracked, and recorded, and document the gaps, risks, and challenges. 
 Recommend and drive a target operating model to scale and expand transactions through these vehicles. 
 Define the standards, playbooks, controls, and SOPs that turn contract management into a repeatable discipline. 
 Actively pursue opportunities to grow revenue and transaction volume through existing contract vehicles, and evaluate the fit of new ones. 
 Systems, Data & Governance  
 Partner with technical business system owners to define how contracts, pricing, and obligations should be structured and recorded in CRM and related systems. 
 Establish data standards, naming conventions, and workflows so contract data is accurate, complete, and reportable. 
 Guide system enhancements, configuration, and automation that support contract governance and reduce manual effort. 
 Ensure records remain audit-ready and aligned with internal governance and external compliance requirements. 
 Cross-Functional Collaboration  
 Collaborate with Legal, Finance, Sales, Pricing, Product, and Operations to align contract execution with commercial and compliance goals. 
 Advise leadership on contract strategy, risk exposure, and expansion opportunities. 
 Coordinate reviews and approvals across stakeholders and keep them informed of obligations and achievement. 
 Reporting & Compliance  
 Produce reporting and dashboards on contract performance, obligations, renewals, and compliance status. 
 Monitor key metrics, service levels, and deadlines, and escalate risks proactively. 
 Maintain the documentation, templates, and job aids that support consistent contract management.

 2+ years in contract management, commercial or deal operations, public-sector or government contracting, or a related discipline, at a lead level. 
 Demonstrated ability to assess current-state processes and design scalable, well-governed operating models. 
 Strong cross-functional stakeholder management, including working directly with IT and business system owners. 
 Experience translating contract requirements into system configuration, data standards, and reporting. 
 Excellent communication, organization, and attention to detail. 
 Bachelor’s degree, Master’s degree or MBA considered an asset. 
 An asset if you have: 
 Direct, hands-on experience managing public-sector contract vehicles and cooperative purchasing agreements. 
 Experience with Microsoft Dynamics CRM and a CPQ or ERP platform. 
 Familiarity with contract lifecycle management (CLM) tools and documentation practices. 
 Working knowledge of public-sector compliance obligations, including reporting, eligibility, and pricing rules. 
 Advanced Microsoft Excel and Power BI reporting skills. 
 Change-management or process-transformation experience.

 Contract lifecycle management 
 Public-sector and government contracting 
 Process assessment and operating-model design 
 Systems and data governance 
 Cross-functional stakeholder management 
 Pricing and compliance governance 
 Reporting and analytics 
 Business partnering and influence

 Public-sector contracts are managed consistently and compliantly, with audit-ready documentation. 
 A clear current-state assessment and an agreed target operating model are delivered and adopted. 
 Contract data is accurately structured and recorded in business systems, enabling reliable reporting. 
 Revenue, transaction volume, and coverage through these contract vehicles grow in line with organizational goals. 
 Manual effort is reduced through improved processes, standards, and automation.

 Attractive compensation package

 Work-life balance with a flexible working schedule

Mission of this Role
 The Strategy Manager is the senior operational layer of Foundation's strategy practice. This role exists to own client relationships at the oversight level, develop the strategists beneath them, and free VP-level leadership to operate on business growth, team architecture, and company direction.
 The Strategy Manager is accountable for strategic quality across a $2M+ book of business, acts as the primary escalation point for their assigned accounts, and takes full ownership of the people leadership gap that currently sits between individual strategists and VP-level oversight. They are expected to hold positions, defend recommendations under pressure, and grow the capabilities of their team without waiting to be asked.
 Key Responsibilities
 Own the Client Oversight Relationship
 Serve as the senior point of contact for each account in your book, building and maintaining relationships with budget decision-makers and senior client stakeholders.
 Act as the primary escalation owner when strategic direction is challenged, client expectations are at risk, or a situation requires a more senior voice.
 Host strategy presentations, sell the direction, and hold your ground under pushback. Clients should feel they have a senior strategic partner, not just access to a team.
 Maintain a clear, current view of account health across your entire book, surfacing risks to the VP of Strategy before they become problems.
 Drive Strategic Quality Across Your Book
 Oversee GEO and content strategy execution across every account you own, ensuring work is aligned with the defined strategic direction and meeting client-specific KPIs.
 Provide meaningful oversight review on strategic deliverables including content plans, QBRs, and monthly reporting, identifying drift, outdated assumptions, or missed opportunities.
 Bring a GEO-first lens to every account. You should be fluent in generative and answer engine optimization, and it should show in how you review and elevate the work.
 Partner with Account Management on each shared client to ensure contracts, upselling, and cross-team coordination are handled cleanly and strategically.
 Lead and Develop the Team
 Manage 3-5 strategists with real accountability for their development, not just their output. Build meaningful PDPs, run structured 1:1s, and move people along the specialist-to-strategist path.
 Coach strategists on call confidence, client communication, and the ability to own and defend strategic positions. The most common development gap on this team is deference; your job is to close it.
 Score and review strategist client calls using the Foundation performance rubric, delivering specific, actionable feedback that names patterns and sets expectations.
 Develop team GEO capability. Ensure the strategists you lead can articulate and execute generative engine optimization with confidence, not just describe it.
 Flag performance concerns to the VP of Strategy early, with supporting evidence, rather than waiting for a formal review cycle.
 Support Revenue Growth and Account Expansion
 Identify upsell and expansion opportunities within your book and route them to Account Management with a clear strategic rationale.
 Participate in strategic sales conversations for new accounts where your subject matter expertise adds credibility and conversion value.
 Contribute to Foundation's GEO positioning by staying current on platform shifts, citation behavior, and AI-search trends, and by surfacing what matters to the wider team.
 You Might Be a Fit If You...
 Have moved past legacy SEO and actively build content and GEO strategies for generative and answer engine visibility, not as an add-on but as a core discipline.
 Are fluent in B2B and SaaS/tech client relationships, where the funnel, the stakeholder dynamic, and the sales motion are fundamentally different from B2C.
 Can hold a position under pressure. You present, defend, and close on strategy recommendations in front of senior client stakeholders without defaulting to hedging or deferral.
 Want to build people, not just manage them. You have real examples of growing a direct report's capability, not just a willingness to try it.
 Are ready to lead a team before you feel completely ready. You default to ownership, not escalation.
 Required Experience
 5+ years in digital strategy, content strategy, or multi-channel marketing strategy, with at least 2 years in a senior or oversight capacity.
 Demonstrated experience managing or meaningfully developing at least one direct report.
 Proven GEO fluency: you have built and delivered content strategies designed for AI-driven answer engines and can speak to it with authority.
 Strong B2B or SaaS/tech client portfolio, with experience presenting and defending strategy at the VP or Director level.
 Strong analytical capabilities across digital platforms such as Google Analytics, Search Console, Ahrefs, and HubSpot.
 Exceptional ability to communicate complex strategic direction with precision and confidence, in writing and in real-time client conversation.
 Metrics / KPIs

 Target: Zero unmanaged escalations. Post-Strategy NPS of 8 or above (internal and external). Retention rate across your oversight book remains positive.

 Target: Strategic deliverables across your book are delivered on time, clearly structured, and to spec. Oversight review catches drift before client delivery, not after.

 Target: Each direct report has an active PDP reviewed monthly. At least one strategist advances measurably on a named development gap per quarter, as evidenced by rubric scores and call review data.
 4. GEO Execution Quality
 Target: GEO strategies recommended across your book reflect current platform behavior and best practice. Accounts influenced by GEO-informed strategic pivots show measurable improvement in AI citation visibility within 90-180 days.
 5. Revenue Contribution
 Target: Commission tied directly to expansion within your oversight book. Upsell opportunities are identified proactively and routed to Account Management with clear strategic rationale, not flagged after the fact.

 Taiga est une entreprise canadienne qui réinvente l'environnement des sports motorisés grâce à des véhicules électriques hors route révolutionnaires. Adoptant une approche d'ingénierie optimisée, Taiga repousse les frontières de la technologie électrique pour atteindre des rapports puissance-poids extrêmes et les spécifications thermiques nécessaires afin de surpasser les véhicules de sports motorisés à combustion haute performance comparables.  Nous  embauchons  un  développeur   logiciel   embarqué  pour  concevoir  et  maintenir  le  logiciel  IoT qui  alimente  les  véhicules   connectés  de Taiga.  Construit  des  systèmes   fiables  :   écrit  du code propre et  maintenable  pour des  plateformes   embarquées   fonctionnant  dans des conditions  réelles .

 Collaboration et qualité

 Compétences   essentielles

3 à 5 ans d’expérience en développement de logiciels embarqués.

 Atouts

 L’occasion  de  jouer  un  rôle   clé  dans la  définition  de  l’avenir  de  l’exploration   en  plein air pour  une  marque de  véhicules   électriques  de premier plan.   
 La chance de  travailler  avec  une  équipe  passionnée , collaborative et  motivée ,  déterminée  à  repousser  les  limites  et à  relever  des  défis   ambitieux  ensemble.

The Role   
 At Treewalk, you’ll own the entire public-company reporting cycle: fast closes, MD&A storytelling, IFRS/US GAAP judgment calls, and scalable system design. You’ll own end-to-end financial disclosure for a portfolio of high growth clients in life sciences, including pharmaceuticals, therapeutics, and other applications of biosciences and biotechnology. Many engagements will tap you as a de-facto fractional CFO, guiding strategy as well as disclosure; others will lean on you as the go-to technical expert. Either way, every file is yours to run. 
 Deadlines are real; overtime isn’t a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility—so your evenings stay yours. 
 If you’ve led pub-co audits at a small- to mid-size firm or managed reporting inside a listed issuer, and you’re ready to trade 70-hour busy-season marathons for high-impact work, tangible ownership, and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you. 
 How You’ll Create Impact Day-to-Day 
 Own the story behind the numbers: Draft and polish quarterly and annual financial statements and MD&A that stand up to capital-markets scrutiny and tell each client’s growth narrative from the science, to the milestones, and the financial commitments required to achieve the business objectives.
 Make R&D spend make sense: Advise clients on accounting for research and development costs, clinical and pre-clinical trial accruals, CRO/CDMO arrangements, and measuring burn rate against progress.
 Master the technical hurdles: Tackle complex issues such as licensing and collaboration agreements, milestone and royalty revenue, acquired IPR&D, government grants and funding, intangible assets and impairment, and package them into robust technical memos and disclosures.
 Untangle complex capital structures: Work through warrants, convertible instruments, derivative liabilities, royalty and streaming financings, unit offerings, debt/equity splits, and stock-based compensation.
 Run the engine of multi-entity groups: Build rock-solid consolidation and foreign-currency translation models that make complex structures look effortless.
 Turn data into insight: Deliver sharp balance sheet and P&L analyses, spotlighting trends and red-flag variances before anyone else sees them.
 Keep leadership laser-focused: Produce monthly variance reports against forecasts and annual plans, translating the findings into clear, action-ready recommendations, including cash runway and financing timing.
 Shape the roadmap: Guide annual budgets and rolling forecasts, aligning stakeholders around targets that push the business without breaking it.
 Step in as the “extra brain”: Handle special-project bookkeeping or period-end close entries when clients need a fractional controller’s precision and speed.
 Make audits painless: Design year-end audit plans, prep airtight support, and quarterback conversations with external auditors so CEOs and CFOs can sleep at night.
 Guard continuous disclosure: Stay ahead of regulatory changes, draft timely filings, and ensure nothing slips through the cracks on SEDAR+ or EDGAR.
 Build and grow the industry service line: Take ownership of the practice area and scale it, and develop the people who will run alongside you. 
 Result: clients see you as the calm, expert voice who keeps them compliant and strategic, while you build Treewalk’s Biotechnology and Life Sciences service line without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate... 
 CPA designation required.
 Significant public company audit and/or financial reporting experience, serving or working within pre-revenue or early-commercial biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or other life sciences reporting issuers listed in Canada and/or the US.
 Hands-on technical depth in life sciences accounting and fluency in the drug and product development lifecycle.
 After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost for strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Why Treewalk Feels Different 
 It’s Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.
 No-Strings Learning Fund: We pay 100% of your CPA modules, annual dues, and any pro-dev courses you choose, and we’ll never claw it back if you move on.
 Freedom Over Face-Time: Own your deadlines, shape your schedule. Hit a midday workout, do the school run. Just bring the results.
 Day-One Peace of Mind: Extended health, dental, vision, and parental-leave benefits start the moment you join.
 Who We Are 
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born, scaling nationwide, and obsessed with turning capital-markets complexity into clarity. We give TSX, TSX-V, CSE, NASDAQ, and OTC issuers an end-to-end disclosure engine, so they can focus on growth while we keep them bullet-proof in the spotlight.
 But labels like “accounting firm” don’t capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:
 Holacracy over hierarchy: Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.
 Sector depth, startup curiosity: If it’s innovative, we’re already in it, or will be tomorrow.
 Growth at warp speed: One of Canada’s fastest-rising advisory practices, we set audacious goals, then sprint past them.
 Training ground for tomorrow’s CFOs: Whether you’re a seasoned audit manager or a life sciences controller, Treewalk is where accountants level up for industry roles and capital-markets strategy.
 The Values That Power Us 
 Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
 Support: No one goes it alone. Collaboration is our default setting.
 Ownership: We celebrate wins and own slip-ups with equal conviction.
 Kaizen: Continuous improvement isn’t a buzzword; it’s our daily operating system.
 Annual Salary: $125,000

The successful candidate will bring hands-on experience with Medidata Rave EDC and C# programming to develop custom functions, support database configurations, and contribute to clinical database programming activities independently. Design, build, test, and maintain clinical study databases throughout the study lifecycle.

Develop, program, and test custom functions using C# to support Medidata Rave EDC functionality.
Create annotated electronic Case Report Forms (eCRFs) and program automated edit checks to support data validation.
Develop and test files required for electronic data uploads, data transfers, and integrations.
Program and generate clinical data listings and project tracking reports to support ongoing studies.
Manage database access, process change request (CR) publishing requests, and archive electronic data and documentation upon study completion.
Troubleshoot and resolve database programming issues, providing technical expertise and support to internal teams and sponsors.
Communicate database setup progress, project milestones, and technical issues to internal and external stakeholders.
Contribute to the development and improvement of database programming processes and departmental procedures.

Hands-on experience with Medidata Rave EDC, including clinical database development, configuration, and maintenance.
Proficiency in C# programming, with the ability to independently develop, test, and troubleshoot custom functions within Medidata Rave EDC.
Experience developing and maintaining electronic Case Report Forms (eCRFs) and automated edit checks.
Knowledge of clinical database programming processes, including data transfers, electronic data uploads, and reporting.
Experience generating clinical data listings and project tracking reports.
Strong technical troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently address database programming challenges.
